slices.candidate_source: One fixed TileLang T.prim_func elementwise candidate, then one small candidate using T.Kernel extents plus an explicit scope/layout/swizzle schedule.
slices.independent_schedule_control: The second candidate changes TileLang grid/thread and memory-scope/layout policy without an msl-bundle HostTilingPlan or a ShapeForge GeometryPair template. A semantically equivalent MSL candidate is used only as a correctness oracle comparison, not as a lowering stage.
slices.build: Resolve TileLang 0.1.15 commit a35f8ddf45eba16c21211ec8822d56ce5363036f and TileLang/TVM 4211874e9e4b8770fd20ad0d98ab80afd1df5028 in an isolated worker; record the source digest, frontend/options, lowered host/device modules, per-kernel MSL and runtime identity before execution.
slices.execution: Compile the frontend output in Build, then bind actual buffers and grid/block extents through the shared Metal substrate. The TVM MetalRawStream external-command-buffer mechanism is a design lead only; actual ShapeForge encode/commit/wait evidence must be implemented and audited.
required_positive_evidence: source-only parse/lowering artifact identity precedes any device execution
correct output and read_write final state under tolerances + scaled_error
actual grid/threadgroups/buffer bindings match the frozen TileLang launch metadata
input-dependent TileLang planning is charged to candidate E2E and does not rerun as first JIT during timing
required_negative_evidence: arbitrary host Python outside the proven declarative/sandbox boundary is rejected
calling or importing msl-single/msl-bundle candidate contracts or adapters is rejected
a timed first compilation, cross-Track cache hit, stale frontend version or self-reported launch is rejected
unsupported TileLang syntax/capability returns typed unsupported_contract_capability rather than a crash
slices.current_blocker: This is a specification only. Embedded-code isolation, local frontend installation and actual shared-substrate execution have not been demonstrated.

slices.candidate_source: One fixed Halide Generator elementwise pipeline, then one small pipeline with an explicit GPU block/thread/vector schedule.
slices.independent_schedule_control: The second candidate changes the Halide schedule and generated launch metadata without a HostTilingPlan, msl-bundle geometry file or shared per-task tiler. A semantically equivalent MSL candidate is an oracle comparison only.
slices.build: Resolve Halide 22.1.0 commit a8c592b056c06eeeeb064778e6f83e3c6002338f and its supported LLVM in an isolated worker; AOT-lower the Generator and record generator/schedule identity, host object/header, generated MSL, and (if the configured Apple toolchain path is selected) real AIR/metallib bytes before execution.
slices.execution: Bind the independent Halide-generated device artifact and actual block/thread extents into the shared Metal substrate. Do not call the stock Halide queue/runtime as a black-box evaluator; its ownership of command buffers and timing must not bypass ShapeForge.
required_positive_evidence: AOT build artifacts and frontend/compiler/options identity are frozen before execution
correct output and read_write final state under tolerances + scaled_error
actual Halide block/thread dispatch and buffer permissions are independently observed
Generator and input-dependent scheduling work remain inside the required candidate timing boundary
required_negative_evidence: arbitrary C++/Python generator execution outside the proven sandbox is rejected
using Halide's stock runtime to hide command buffers, host work or self-reported timing is rejected
substituting generated MSL for the Halide candidate identity or invoking an existing MSL Track adapter is rejected
a timed first compile, frontend/LLVM drift, cache sharing or unsupported schedule returns a typed refusal
slices.current_blocker: This is a specification only. Embedded-code isolation, local frontend/LLVM compatibility and the AOT-to-shared-substrate execution seam have not been demonstrated.
